official_sources.title: EA Time Stamped DTM vertical accuracy
official_sources.finding: Environment Agency reports Time Stamped DTM vertical accuracy as +/-15 cm RMSE, not as a per-cell guaranteed maximum error.

official_sources.title: EA Time Stamped DTM datum and units
official_sources.finding: DTM elevations are delivered in metres referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn and aligned to the OS Grid.

official_sources.title: EA DTM multi-resolution archive
official_sources.finding: Time Stamped DTM is available at 25 cm, 50 cm, 1 m and 2 m depending on project requirements, so resolution is a separate provenance field from RMSE.

official_sources.title: EA DSM accuracy is not terrain-only accuracy
official_sources.finding: DSM carries the same stated +/-15 cm RMSE but includes objects, showing that accuracy metadata alone cannot establish bare-earth semantic suitability.

official_sources.title: EA transformation period dependency
official_sources.finding: Environment Agency states that the transformation used is specific to the survey time period and directs users to metadata catalogues for the specific transformation/geoidal model.

official_sources.title: USGS current absolute vertical accuracy
official_sources.finding: Current USGS Lidar Base Specification requires absolute vertical accuracy assessment for both point data and final DEM using ASPRS 2024 methodology.

official_sources.title: USGS NVA DEM assessment
official_sources.finding: Nonvegetated vertical accuracy for the DEM is assessed by comparing checkpoints to the final bare-earth surface.

official_sources.title: USGS VVA DEM assessment
official_sources.finding: Vegetated vertical accuracy for the DEM is separately assessed and reported, preventing a single project RMSE from describing every land-cover regime.

official_sources.title: USGS checkpoint survey error inclusion
official_sources.finding: USGS specifies that NVA RMSEv includes survey error under ASPRS 2024, so checkpoint uncertainty must not be independently added again without checking the reporting basis.

official_sources.title: USGS QL0 absolute vertical RMSEv
official_sources.finding: USGS Table 4 gives QL0 nonvegetated absolute vertical RMSEv <=0.050 m.

official_sources.title: USGS QL1 absolute vertical RMSEv
official_sources.finding: USGS Table 4 gives QL1 nonvegetated absolute vertical RMSEv <=0.100 m.

official_sources.title: USGS QL2 absolute vertical RMSEv
official_sources.finding: USGS Table 4 gives QL2 nonvegetated absolute vertical RMSEv <=0.100 m.

official_sources.title: USGS QL3 absolute vertical RMSEv
official_sources.finding: USGS Table 4 gives QL3 nonvegetated absolute vertical RMSEv <=0.200 m.

official_sources.title: USGS relative vertical precision
official_sources.finding: USGS separately reports smooth-surface and swath-overlap RMSDv, distinguishing relative/internal precision from absolute vertical accuracy.

official_sources.title: USGS QL density not sufficient for accuracy
official_sources.finding: USGS explains that higher point density without meeting the vertical accuracy requirement does not elevate a project to the higher quality level.

official_sources.title: USGS standard deviation versus accuracy
official_sources.finding: USGS defines standard deviation as precision rather than accuracy because it does not account for uncorrected systematic errors.

official_sources.title: USGS standard uncertainty semantics
official_sources.finding: USGS glossary describes standard uncertainty as uncertainty expressed as a standard deviation, supporting explicit uncertainty-basis labels.

official_sources.title: USGS VVA percentile semantics
official_sources.finding: VVA is based on a 95th percentile in vegetated terrain where errors may not be normally distributed.

official_sources.title: USGS 2025 VVA reporting change
official_sources.finding: USGS revision history records that VVA is reported rather than used as a project pass/fail requirement under the updated standard.

official_sources.title: USGS RMSE terminology update
official_sources.finding: Current USGS terminology replaced RMSEz with RMSEv and references ASPRS 2024, so uncertainty reports must pin the standard version and terminology.

official_sources.title: ASPRS second edition status
official_sources.finding: ASPRS publishes the second edition positional accuracy standard as the current modular industry standard referenced by USGS.

official_sources.title: USGS ASPRS 2024 migration
official_sources.finding: USGS documents migration to ASPRS second edition, including revised RMSE terminology and removal of the former 95% confidence-level reporting basis from Table 4.

official_sources.title: OSGM15 Great Britain standard error
official_sources.finding: Ordnance Survey reports OSGM15 standard error of 0.008 m for Great Britain.

official_sources.title: OSGM15 error excludes GNSS
official_sources.finding: OS explicitly states OSGM15 errors exclude GNSS heighting errors, so those components cannot be collapsed into one number without provenance.

official_sources.title: OS regional OSGM15 error variation
official_sources.finding: OSGM15 standard error varies by regional height datum, so the target region must be known before assigning a model uncertainty.

official_sources.title: OS local relative OSGM15 error
official_sources.finding: OS states the relative OSGM15 error introduced within a 10 km extent is only a few millimetres, distinct from absolute model error.

official_sources.title: OS GNSS height example
official_sources.finding: OS notes GNSS height accuracy can be about 2 cm standard error under a specific four-hour high-quality observation example; this is observation-method dependent, not a universal constant.

official_sources.title: EPSG 7711 operation accuracy metadata
official_sources.finding: EPSG:7711 records transformation accuracy 0.008 m; this is operation metadata, not measured target DTM or parcel-height accuracy.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster scale offset semantics
official_sources.finding: GDAL raster bands may carry scale and offset metadata used to transform stored values into meaningful values, which is a separate numeric interpretation dependency.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster unit metadata
official_sources.finding: GDAL raster bands may carry a unit name such as the linear unit for elevation, so uncertainty components must be normalized to the same unit before combination.

official_sources.title: GDAL unscale physical-value equation
official_sources.finding: GDAL unscale applies physical_value = stored_value * scale + offset, meaning storage-domain precision and physical-domain precision must not be conflated.

official_sources.title: GDAL Float32 conversion behavior
official_sources.finding: GDAL unscale defaults many source types including Float32 to Float32 output, while Float64 stays Float64, making numeric representation part of an auditable uncertainty/precision ledger.

official_sources.title: GDAL nodata separate from valid values
official_sources.finding: GDAL defines nodata values and masks separately from valid pixels; nodata must not be converted into an uncertainty contribution or an elevation value.

official_sources.title: USGS accuracy error dictionary provenance
official_sources.finding: USGS maintains standardized vertical-accuracy error terminology for checkpoint review, supporting explicit error-source classification rather than a single opaque score.
